free_tier.stated: No published total storage cap. 15 GB per file standard, 30 GB for Premium/monetised channels; up to 8 hours duration.

egress.terms: Free — Rumble serves its own CDN, no egress billing.

tooling: yt-dlp `Rumble`, `RumbleChannel`, `RumbleEmbed` extractors (verified present). No public upload API; upload is web-only.
chaining: Unlimited files x unlimited accounts at 15 GB each. No documented daily cap, which is unusual and useful.
limits_note: 15 GB/file is mid-tier. Upload is web-form only — this is the automation blocker, since yt-dlp solves retrieval but nothing solves programmatic upload.
reliability_note: rumble.com/faq returned 404/504/410 on three fetch attempts from this network; the 15 GB figure is third-party (kompozy.io, allplatforms.io) rather than a page I could read on Rumble's own domain.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: 'Rumble max file size: 15 GB per upload' (third-party, claims last verified 2026-05-22)
unverified: rumble.com/faq and rumble.com/pricing returned 404/410/504 — blocked/unavailable, no first-party page read

notes: No published total storage cap. 15 GB per file standard, 30 GB for Premium/monetised channels; up to 8 hours duration.
binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
